title: Driver, Conductor Arrested After Teenager Gang-Raped Inside Moving Sleeper Bus Near Delhi
excerpt: A 16-year-old stranded in heavy rain was lured onto an empty sleeper bus in Greater Noida and assaulted during a 47-km ride to Kashmere Gate; both accused arrested the same day.
body:
• A 16-year-old girl from Uttar Pradesh was allegedly gang-raped by the driver and conductor of an empty sleeper bus near Delhi on August 4; both accused have been arrested
  • The teenager was stranded at Pari Chowk in Greater Noida during heavy rain when the accused offered her a ride, claiming they were heading to her destination
  • The bus traveled approximately 47 km from Pari Chowk to Kashmere Gate while the crime was concealed behind curtained sleeper berths
  • The case has been registered under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the POCSO Act; the bus has been seized for forensic examination

Delhi Police have arrested the driver and conductor of a sleeper bus after a 16-year-old girl was allegedly gang-raped inside the moving vehicle during a 47-kilometer ride from Greater Noida to central Delhi earlier this month, in a case that has drawn comparisons to the 2012 Nirbhaya assault and reignited debate over women's safety on India's roads.

How It Happened

The incident occurred on the night of August 4, though it came to public attention on August 31. According to police, the teenager — a Class 11 student from Mainpuri district in Uttar Pradesh — had left home without informing her family after a disagreement and was traveling to her cousin's residence in Noida Sector 63.

Due to heavy rain and darkness, she mistakenly got off at Pari Chowk in Greater Noida around 9 p.m., roughly 25 km from her intended destination. Stranded and unable to find transport, she flagged down an approaching sleeper bus. The vehicle had no passengers — it was returning empty from a workshop in Surajpur where it had undergone repairs.

"The conductor, identified by police as 26-year-old Sandeep, allegedly told the girl the bus was heading toward Noida Sector 63."

The conductor, identified by police as 26-year-old Sandeep, allegedly told the girl the bus was heading toward Noida Sector 63. She boarded. The bus, operated by Vishwanath Travels, was equipped with berths covered by curtains — a standard feature of long-distance sleeper coaches designed for overnight journeys.

The Assault and Aftermath

Shortly after the bus began moving, the conductor allegedly began behaving inappropriately toward the teenager. According to her statement to police, both the conductor and the driver — 39-year-old Kuldeep — sexually assaulted her and threatened to kill her if she resisted. The curtained interior of the sleeper bus concealed the crime from anyone outside.

The bus traveled approximately 47 km before the accused abandoned the girl near Ring Road, close to the Kashmere Gate Interstate Bus Terminal in north Delhi, late that night. The teenager, with the help of a woman constable, approached the Kashmere Gate police station and reported the incident.

Swift Arrest

Delhi Police formed teams, traced the accused, and arrested both Kuldeep and Sandeep the same day from a bus parking area in Timarpur, north Delhi. Police said the accused had been employed by Vishwanath Travels, a private travel company, for more than two years.

The sleeper bus has been seized and sent for forensic examination, where strands of the victim's hair were recovered, according to police. CCTV footage from the entire Pari Chowk-to-Kashmere Gate route is being examined to establish the sequence of events. DCP North District Niharika Bhat confirmed the arrests and said further investigation is underway.

The case has been registered under Section 70(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, which pertains to gang rape of a person under 18, along with provisions of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act and Section 351(3) of the BNS related to criminal intimidation.

Safety Questions Resurface

The case has drawn immediate parallels to the December 2012 Nirbhaya case, when a 23-year-old paramedical student was gang-raped and fatally assaulted inside a moving off-duty bus in Delhi by six men including the driver. That attack triggered nationwide protests and led to sweeping changes in India's sexual assault laws through the Justice J.S. Verma Committee recommendations.

Delhi has since strengthened safety provisions for public transport, including mandatory CCTV cameras on buses, GPS tracking, and emergency helplines. But the nature of this latest case — committed inside a private sleeper bus with curtained interiors that shielded the assault from view — raises pointed questions about safety protocols for private operators, particularly those running sleeper coaches.

Police said verification procedures for drivers and conductors of private buses are being intensified. A charge sheet is expected to be filed before the competent court within the statutory deadline under the POCSO Act.
